bihar_raw_news.title: " Bihar to develop around 700 model schools for NEET, JEE preparation": CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: "Bihar to develop around 700 model schools for NEET, JEE preparation": CM Samrat Choudhary ANI 06 Sep 2026, 00:05 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], September 5 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday announced that around 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan Model Schools will be developed across the state to provide students with facilities and academic support for competitive examinations such as NEET and JEE. Addressing the Teacher's Day occasion 2026 at Sri Krishna Memorial Hall here, Choudhary said the proposed university would provide regular training to teachers from primary education to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. 'More than seven lakh teachers are working in Bihar from primary schools to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. To improve the quality of teachers and provide them regular training, a separate Teacher Training University will be established,' the Chief Minister said. Choudhary also announced that Bihar will develop a modern artificial intelligence ecosystem in collaboration with leading technology companies such as Google, Microsoft and Sarvam AI. 'Teachers will be provided training in the latest artificial intelligence technologies,' he said. An MoU was signed between the Bihar Education Department and Google during the programme for training teachers in AI and modern technologies. The Chief Minister said efforts would also be made to establish a centre of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Bihar to provide better higher education opportunities to students. On examination reforms, Choudhary said the government aims to release matriculation examination results within seven days of completion of the examination. Students dissatisfied with their marks would be allowed to reappear within 15 days in designated examination slots, he said. He added that arrangements were being developed to release engineering and polytechnic results within 24 hours. A committee headed by a sitting High Court judge has been constituted to suggest structural reforms in the examination system, Choudhary said, adding that the government would act on its recommendations. The state is also considering decentralising the examination system and releasing results centre-wise to reduce delays and facilitate timely admissions, he said. The Chief Minister said, 'Around 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan Model Schools would be developed in Bihar, where students would receive facilities to prepare for competitive examinations such as NEET and JEE.' Live online teachers would be made available to students, including those staying in hostels and those commuting from home, enabling them to access academic assistance round the clock, he said. On Bihar's educational heritage, Choudhary said the process of establishing the historic Vikramshila University was being taken forward. 'The land acquisition process for Vikramshila University was completed on July 15, and work to take the project forward on the ground will be undertaken within the next year,' he said. Highlighting improvements in school education, Choudhary said the primary-level dropout rate declined from around 46 per cent in 2004-05 to 2 per cent in 2024-25. bihar_raw_news.title: Shared Peril - The Statesman
bihar_raw_news.content: The catastrophic floods in Nepal should end a dangerous illusion in India: that Himalayan disasters can be neatly contained within national borders or explained simply by blaming an upstream neighbour for “releasing” water. The Himalayan river system does not recognise political boundaries. What happens in Nepal’s mountains can shape the fate of millions in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, just as infrastructure decisions on the Indian side can worsen flooding across Nepal’s Terai. The growing volatility of this shared ecosystem demands a fundamental shift from reactive disaster management to cooperative risk management. India has long treated floods largely as a domestic engineering problem, responding with embankments, barrages, relief camps and compensation. Yet the record suggests that controlling rivers is not the same as understanding them. The 2008 Kosi catastrophe remains an uncomfortable reminder. It was not simply an overwhelming volume of water that devastated Bihar; institutional failure and a breach in an inadequately maintained embankment transformed a manageable river flow into a humanitarian disaster. That distinction matters even more today. Advertisement The Himalayas are producing hazards that increasingly defy the conventional definition of a flood. Cloudbursts, landslides, glacial lake outbursts and rock-and-ice avalanches can unleash torrents carrying enormous quantities of sediment and debris. The 2021 Chamoli disaster and the destruction at Dharali in Uttarakhand last year demonstrated the destructive potential of such events. Nepal’s latest tragedy belongs to the same expanding geography of Himalayan risk. Advertisement Climate change compounds the problem, but invoking it should not become an excuse for institutional fatalism. A warming atmosphere may intensify extreme rainfall, yet human decisions determine much of the eventual damage. Roads and railways obstruct natural drainage; settlements expand across floodplains; embankments deteriorate; hydropower projects proliferate in fragile valleys; and warning systems often fail at the point where they matter most ~ reaching vulnerable communities in time. The India-Nepal relationship consequently needs a more ambitious framework than periodic exchanges of river data. Real-time monitoring must be expanded across vulnerable catchments. Joint forecasting models are needed, along with regular sharing of information on sediment movement, changing river channels, glacial lakes and the structural condition of embankments and barrages. Disaster warnings must also travel beyond government offices to the villages and households directly in harm’s way. This is not merely an environmental issue. North Bihar’s chronic vulnerability affects agriculture, migration, infrastructure and regional economic development. Repeated disasters can trap already poor communities in cycles of asset loss and displacement. The economic consequences of Himalayan instability will increasingly extend far beyond the mountains. The deeper lesson from Nepal is therefore one of interdependence. Neither country can engineer its way to safety independently while sharing rivers whose behaviour is becoming less predictable. The question is no longer whether the next Himalayan disaster will cross a border. It is whether the institutions on both sides will recognise that the border is largely irrelevant to the disaster itself. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said India’s 7.8 percent quarterly growth amid global uncertainty reflects its economic strength. He said India has come a long way, from policy paralysis to policy dynamism. Addressing the gathering at the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the world is watching India become the fastest growing major economy. Prime Minister said Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) has given generations of students the opportunity to learn, grow and make a difference over the years. Mr Modi said the college has distinguished itself over the years, making a mark for academic excellence. He termed the alumni of SRCC as very special and ‘the OGs’. The Prime Minister stated that former Finance Minister Arun Jaitley was an alum of SRCC. He said SRCC alumni have left their mark in every sector, from arts to politics. He added that together, 140 crore Indians will make India both Viksit and Aatmanirbhar. The Prime Minister also said that India has come a long way from policy paralysis to policy dynamism. Mr. Modi also lauded the students of SRCC for taking its glory to the global stage. Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, in his speech, praised SRCC for maintaing its high standard over the years. He said today India is the third largest Start Up ecosystem under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi. He said there is requirement of skilled human resources in the global market. The Minister termed it an opportunity for the young population. Earlier this evening, Prime Minister Modi traveled by the Delhi Metro as he headed to SRCC to participate in the college’s centenary celebrations.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 58 Over 500 investors, finance ministers and business leaders to attend inaugural iBRICS Summit
national_raw_news.content: More than 500 institutional investors, finance ministers and business leaders will participate in the inaugural iBRICS Summit, on the sidelines of BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12th and 13th of this month. The two-day summit is designed to connect sovereign capital with bankable infrastructure, energy, and digital capacity projects across 21 BRICS member states and partner nations. Sovereign wealth funds, pension funds and family offices attending the iBRICS Summit manage a total wealth of 1 trillion US Dollars. They will discuss cross-border investments, non-dollar settlements and payment systems among BRICS economies. Discussions are also expected on linking national fast-payment systems such as India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Brazil’s Pix, along with interoperability between central bank digital currencies. The summit comes at a critical juncture as BRICS economies adapt to shifting trade dynamics, US tariff pressures, and high dollar-clearing costs. The meeting is intended to connect institutional capital with infrastructure, energy and digital projects across BRICS member and partner countries. As BRICS Chair 2026, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Summit will bring together leaders of BRICS Member and Partner Countries as well as Outreach Invitees. India’s BRICS Chairship is guided by the theme: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the Prime Minister’s vision of a people-centric approach rooted in the spirit of “Humanity First”.

national_raw_news.content: Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 Inaugurated, Network Expands To 16 Operational Stations Covering Around 17 Km Infrastructure Indore Metro Priority Corridor–2 Inaugurated, Network Expands To 16 Operational Stations Covering Around 17 Km Swarajya Staff Sep 06, 2026 | Updated 09:24 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Indore Metro priority corridor-2 has been inaugurated (Pic Via PIB) Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav yesterday (5 September) inaugurated the Indore Metro Priority corridor-2 at the Brilliant Convention Centre in Vijay Nagar. Regular passenger services on the expanded Gandhi Nagar-Malviya Nagar Square corridor began today, marking a significant milestone for Madhya Pradesh's commercial capital. The operational network has expanded from approximately 6 km to 17 km, with the extended corridor covering 16 stations. The first train departs at 9 am, while the last train operates at 7 pm, with Metro trains available every 15 minutes and more than 80 trips scheduled daily. The initial 6 km priority section entered operations on 31st May 2025 and was officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi via video conferencing from Bhopal. The new 11 km extension runs from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha, also known as Radisson Square, bringing Metro services closer to key residential and commercial areas across the city. The newly inaugurated phase-I (Reach-II) of approx 11 km comprising 11-stations starting from Super Corridor-3 to Malviya Nagar Chauraha and has been developed at an estimated cost of Rs 2,850 crore. With this expansion, the Indore Metro network now comprises 16 operational stations covering approximately 17 km, with a cumulative project cost of about Rs 4,370 crore. The Asian Development Bank had last year approved a $190 million loan to support development of an 8.62 kilometre underground metro line with seven stations, connecting congested areas to the airport. Chief Minister Yadav said the second phase marked the metro's gradual movement from the outskirts towards more populated parts of Indore, with the planned Yellow Line eventually continuing beyond Malviya Nagar towards Shaheed Bagicha, Khajrana Chauraha, Bengali Chauraha, Patrakar Colony and Palasia before reaching the railway station. The corridor received approval from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety in March 2026.
